title: Enforce action-based authorization across API routers
description: AuthN exists (Keycloak JWT middleware) and an action-based permission model exists (adp.authz.permissions.is_permitted over PERMISSION_GRANTS), but check_permission is called in 0 of 19 routers. The architecture doc claims RBAC governs who can confirm requirements/accept recommendations/override verdicts — currently untrue. Add a FastAPI dependency require_action(ActionType) that resolves get_current_user, calls is_permitted(user.role, action), and raises 403 on denial. Apply it to every mutating route mapped to its ActionType (WRITE_DESIGN, SUBMIT_AI_OPERATION, CONFIRM_RECOMMENDATION, OVERRIDE_VERDICT, ADD_FINDING, EXPORT_DESIGN, AMEND_STANDARD). Retire the mismatched linear require_role dependency in adp/auth/deps.py (the permission table is not a linear hierarchy — REVIEWER can override verdicts but not write designs). Dev/E2E stays green because UNAUTHENTICATED_USER is ENTERPRISE_ARCHITECT (all actions).

title: Business Capability Visualization Suite (heat map, matrix, value-stream mapping, roadmap, dependency graph, bubble chart)
description:
Why: Business capability visualization is a core enterprise architecture deliverable with a well-established set of patterns. ADP already captures the underlying data (business_capabilities, value_streams, value_stream_stages, business_domains, capability_design_links, application registry with capability links -- specs 033-036) but the Business Capabilities page today only has a tree view (web/src/business/CapabilityTree.tsx) -- none of the standard EA visualization patterns exist yet.

Relationship to ADP-914: that epic's expanded scope (canvas -> general Mermaid-DSL diagramming tool) explicitly lists "capability models (business + technical capabilities)" as minimum coverage. Whether these visualizations get built AS Mermaid-DSL diagrams through that future generic canvas, or as dedicated purpose-built views (charts/grids, not diagrams) on the existing Business Capabilities page, is an open design question -- not decided here. Linked as related/parent since they'll likely need to be sequenced together, but this bead exists to capture the specific EA patterns wanted regardless of which implementation path is chosen.

What: six established capability-visualization patterns to build out (scope each individually when picked up; not all need to ship at once -- #1 is the natural MVP):

1. Capability map (heat map) -- the default/most common EA artifact. Hierarchical grid of L1/L2/L3 capabilities (e.g. "Underwriting" -> "Risk Assessment" -> "Rating Engine"), color-coded by a metric: maturity, investment priority, tech debt, or strategic fit. Dense, scannable at a glance.

2. Capability vs. application/system matrix -- rows = capabilities, columns = systems (or vice versa), cells show which apps support which capabilities. Surfaces redundancy (multiple systems supporting the same capability) and gaps (capability with no system support). ADP already has the capability<->application link data (application registry, migration 010+) to drive this directly.

3. Capability-to-value-stream mapping -- shows which capabilities are invoked at each stage of a value stream (e.g. quote -> bind -> policy issuance -> claims). Shows business flow rather than static structure. ADP already has value_streams/value_stream_stages/value_stream_stage_capabilities data to drive this directly.

4. Heat map over time (capability roadmap) -- same grid as #1 but with a horizontal timeline axis, showing planned maturity uplift per capability per quarter/year. Common for transformation programs. Needs a maturity-over-time data shape that likely doesn't exist yet (current data is point-in-time).

5. Capability dependency / relationship graph -- node-link diagram (not a grid) for capabilities with significant cross-dependencies (shared data, shared services) that a flat grid hides. This is the one pattern where a graph layout (e.g. via the Mermaid/canvas path from ADP-914) earns its keep over a matrix -- worth building via that generic diagramming tool rather than a bespoke chart.

6. Bubble/scatter plot (investment vs. maturity, or cost vs. business value) -- two-axis plot, capability as a bubble sized by cost or headcount. Good for prioritization conversations ("high-value but low-maturity" capabilities). ADP already has business_value/investment-adjacent fields on capabilities and cost data on the application side to potentially roll up.

Scope, sequencing, and exact implementation approach (dedicated charting library vs. the ADP-914 generic canvas, which patterns are grid/matrix/chart vs. true diagrams) are all open -- dig deeper when picked up. #1 (capability heat map) is the natural starting point since it's the single most common artifact and the underlying data already exists.

title: Guard against src/api fetch() calls that bypass auth (the black-screen class of bug)
description:
Why: the post-login black screen on the Azure deploy (ADP-cm9, 2026-07-24) was ultimately caused by src/api/application.ts (and src/canvas/Workspace.tsx's CALM export) using a raw fetch() with no Authorization header, so those calls 401'd once auth was enabled in a real deployment. It shipped and reached user testing UNCAUGHT because both the frontend unit/component tests and CI run with VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false -- so a token is never expected and a missing-auth-header call looks fine. The whole authenticated code path is effectively untested.

The correct pattern already exists: src/api/client.ts exposes getAuthHeader() + apiGet/apiMutation, and most api modules (business, portfolio, knowledge, designs, governance, intake, recommend, theme, config, agentReview, chat's SSE) route through it. application.ts was the outlier that reinvented fetch without auth. Nothing mechanically prevents the next module from doing the same.

What (options to weigh at implementation, none decided yet):

1. STATIC GUARD (cheapest, catches it at build/CI): a lint rule or a small unit test that scans src/ for `fetch(` usages under src/api/** (and component files) and asserts each either routes through client.ts's apiGet/apiMutation OR explicitly attaches getAuthHeader(). Mirror the existing boundary-enforcement test pattern already used in the repo (e.g. tests/unit/chat/test_tools_boundary.py on the backend, and the agents toolkit boundary test) but for the web client. An ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule banning bare fetch() outside client.ts is another form.

2. ELIMINATE THE FOOTGUN: make client.ts the ONLY place allowed to call fetch(); refactor application.ts and any other raw-fetch callers to use apiGet/apiMutation (or a shared streaming helper for the SSE/blob cases that can't use apiGet). Removes the class of bug rather than policing it.

3. AUTH-ENABLED E2E SMOKE: a Playwright run with VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=true against a real (or mocked-token) Keycloak that actually logs in and loads the landing page -- would have caught the 401 crash directly. Heavier; the existing e2e suite is route-mocked and auth-off.

Recommend (1) as the immediate low-cost guard (a scan-based unit test is proportionate and fast), optionally (2) as the cleaner long-term shape. (3) is valuable but a bigger lift and overlaps with the broader "no auth-enabled path is exercised in CI" gap.

Scope note: this is test/CI hardening, not a product feature. Not spec'd via speckit.

title: Add a React ErrorBoundary to the web app (no black-screen on unhandled errors)
description:
Why: the frontend has NO React error boundary anywhere in web/src (confirmed via grep for ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch/getDerivedStateFromError). When any component throws -- e.g. an unhandled API error surfacing through React Query, or reading undefined data after a failed fetch -- React unmounts the entire tree, leaving an empty #root. With the dark theme's near-black body background (--bg: #0a0f16, default follows the OS), the result is a completely black screen with no indication of what went wrong.

This is exactly how the ADP-cm9 auth-flag bug manifested for the user: the deployed frontend had VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false baked in (from a leaked web/.env.local), so every API call 401'd, a component threw, and with no boundary the whole app disappeared into a black screen -- giving zero diagnostic signal. The root cause was fixed (.dockerignore + Dockerfile pins VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=true), but the FAILURE MODE remains: any future error (expired token, backend down, a bad deploy) will still black-screen instead of showing something actionable.

What: add a top-level React ErrorBoundary (class component with getDerivedStateFromError + componentDidCatch) wrapping <App/> in web/src/main.tsx (inside AuthProvider/QueryClientProvider or around App). On catch, render a simple themed fallback -- "Something went wrong", the error message, and a reload button -- instead of a blank tree. Consider also a narrower boundary around the main content area so a single page's crash doesn't take down the nav shell.

Scope notes:
- Pair with React Query's error handling: a query error thrown into render (throwOnError) should hit the boundary; decide whether pages use throwOnError or handle errors inline. At minimum the boundary is the last-resort net.
- Log caught errors to console (and later, optionally, to the backend/telemetry) so black-screen incidents leave a trace.
- Not blocking for the immediate redeploy -- the auth fix makes the app render normally -- but strongly recommended so the next failure is diagnosable rather than invisible.
close_reason: Implemented in commit cac1e2c: web/src/ui/ErrorBoundary.tsx wraps App in main.tsx -- unhandled render errors now show a 'Something went wrong' panel + error text + Reload instead of a black screen. Proved its value immediately during the ADP-cm9 debugging (turned the final 401 crash into a readable error).

title: Architecture-as-code: make Postgres-captured data (business arch, applications, designs, etc.) available as versioned files, not just DB rows
description:
Why: "Architecture as code" is a core project principle, but a considerable amount of what ADP now captures (business capabilities, value streams, domains, applications, tech tags, designs, chat) lives only in Postgres — not in git, not directly readable by an AI/tool without DB access. That's a gap against the stated principle: all captured information should be available to AI to easily read and understand, as versioned, diffable files.

Context already in the codebase: ADP-SPEC-011's export bundle (adp.export.bundle.ExportOrchestrator) already proves the pattern — it atomically writes a single design's ArchitectureDescription to a git-tracked model.json + docs. It's narrow today: one design at a time, manually triggered via a confirmation_id gate, C4-designs only (doesn't cover business capabilities/value streams/domains/applications/tech tags, all added in specs 029-041 after 011 shipped).

Options discussed 2026-07-23 (none decided — dig deeper when picked up):

1. RECOMMENDED STARTING POINT: Postgres stays the interactive source of truth; extend the existing export orchestrator (or a sibling) to run continuously/automatically across ALL domains, not just designs -- one JSON file per entity into a predictable architecture/ tree, committed to git automatically (on write, or debounced/scheduled). AI and humans read architecture straight from the repo; every change is a reviewable diff. Main risk: if the export lags or silently fails, the git files go stale and become actively misleading -- reliability of the sync (ideally same-transaction or a fast async trigger with a freshness check) is the real engineering problem, not the JSON serialization.

2. Flip source of truth: JSON/YAML in git becomes canonical, Postgres becomes a rebuildable index/cache -- same pattern this project already uses for Keycloak's realm config (infra/keycloak/adp-realm.json imported into a live instance). Philosophically purest, but a much bigger rewrite of every write path, and pgvector hybrid search + audit trail still need a real database underneath -- Postgres doesn't disappear, it changes role.

3. Drop Postgres entirely, work only in JSON. Not recommended: hybrid search (pgvector + full-text via adp.search), multi-table traceability joins (capability<->design<->application links), audit integrity, and concurrent-write handling are real, working capabilities today that plain files would mean reimplementing badly, for an unclear purity win.

Scope, exact file layout, sync mechanism, and which option (or hybrid) to pursue are all open -- this bead exists to capture the direction and the options so they aren't lost, not to commit to an approach yet.

title: Security model review post-Azure-deployment + CI security tooling gaps
description:
Why: ADP now has real internet-facing attack surface (adp-api external
ingress, the OIDC CI/CD trust chain, ACR-hosted images, Bicep IaC) that
didn't exist before ADP-fnv. Time to review the security model end to end
and close CI tooling gaps rather than assume existing coverage is enough.

What already exists (confirmed by reading the actual CI workflow/config,
not assumed):
  - bandit (Python SAST) and pip-audit (Python dependency CVE scan) run in
    .github/workflows/drift-check.yml (QG-06/QG-07).
  - OWASP ZAP API DAST scan (zap-api-scan job), thresholds in .zap/rules.tsv
    (40018 SQLi intentionally WARN, a known false-positive -- see bd memory
    zap-sqli-40018-is-warn-by-decision).
  - New Azure CI/CD (ADP-fnv.10) already follows good practice: OIDC
    federated credential (no stored client secret), RBAC scoped to only
    AcrPush + Container Apps Contributor on adp-rg, ACR admin user disabled
    (managed-identity pull only), Key Vault RBAC-authorized secrets.

CONFIRMED GAPS (checked directly, not guessed):
  1. Frontend dependency scanning: NONE. 'npm audit --audit-level=high' in
     web/ currently reports 8 vulnerabilities (3 moderate, 2 high, 3
     critical) and nothing in CI gates on this -- only Python deps
     (pip-audit) are checked. Add an npm audit (or better, a combined
     tool -- see below) step to drift-check.yml.
  2. GitHub-native repo security features are OFF: checked via
     'gh api repos/muirjc/ADP' -- secret_scanning, secret_scanning_push_
     protection, and dependabot_security_updates are all null (disabled);
     'gh api repos/muirjc/ADP/vulnerability-alerts' returns 404 (Dependabot
     alerts not enabled either). These are free, zero-maintenance,
     GitHub-native -- turn them on via repo Settings > Security (or
     'gh api' PATCH) rather than building custom tooling for what GitHub
     already offers.
  3. No IaC scanning for the new infra/azure/*.bicep files -- nothing
     checks for Azure misconfigurations (e.g. Checkov, or `az bicep`'s own
     linter which is correctness-only, not security-focused).
  4. No container image scanning -- the two Dockerfiles (repo root,
     infra/keycloak/) produce images pushed to ACR with no CVE scan of OS
     packages/layers. Trivy is the obvious free option (can run in CI
     against the built image before push, or ACR has native Defender for
     Cloud image scanning as a paid alternative).
  5. No CodeQL (or Semgrep) -- bandit is Python-only and lighter-weight;
     CodeQL covers Python + the TS/JS frontend in one setup and is free for
     the visibility level this repo has.

Scope for this task: (a) do the actual security model review (auth flows,
secret handling, network exposure -- adp-api external/Keycloak internal/
Postgres private already looks right per ADP-fnv's own design, worth
re-confirming end to end rather than re-deriving from memory), (b) turn on
the free GitHub-native features (#2) first since they're zero-effort,
(c) add npm audit + Trivy + a Bicep scanner to CI, (d) evaluate CodeQL.
Prioritize free/native tooling over new paid services given this is a
personal/small-scale deployment.

Not yet spec'd via /speckit-specify -- security/ops hardening work, tracked
here rather than as an ADP-SPEC-NNN feature.
notes:
Phase 0 (verify existing controls) -- all green: Postgres still fully private (VNet-injection, no public access), Keycloak still internal-only ingress, API still external, ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=true on the live revision (no drift), OIDC service principal RBAC still scoped to exactly AcrPush+Container Registry Tasks Contributor (ACR) + Container Apps Contributor (adp-rg), federated credential still scoped to repo:...:ref:refs/heads/main only, no secrets in ARM deployment history, authz completeness test + full suite green, no CORS middleware (confirmed correct by design).

Phase 1 (GitHub-native toggles) -- repo was personal-account-owned (muirjc/ADP), which blocks secret scanning regardless of plan tier. User transferred the repo to the CampbellConsultingGroup org (GitHub Team plan) to unlock it -- required fixing the OIDC federated credential subject (repo:muirjc/ADP -> repo:CampbellConsultingGroup/ADP) and the local git remote afterward. Result: Dependabot alerts + security updates + secret scanning all enabled successfully. Push protection + CodeQL default-setup deferred -- both need the separate GitHub Advanced Security add-on (per-committer billing), user chose not to opt in for now.

Phase 2 (Keycloak realm tightening) -- found a much bigger issue than planned while doing this: (1) infra/keycloak/adp-realm.json's redirectUris/webOrigins were still "*" wildcards, AND (2) web/.env's local-dev VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 was shipping unmodified into the production frontend bundle (Vite bakes env vars at build time, nothing overrode it) -- meaning real end-user login had likely never worked in any deployment this epic produced. Root architecture problem: Keycloak has internal-only ingress but keycloak-js's login flow requires the browser to reach Keycloak directly.

Fix (user chose "reverse-proxy through adp-api" over exposing Keycloak externally): new adp.api.routers.auth_proxy transparently proxies /auth/* on adp-api (already public) to internal Keycloak. Keycloak reconfigured with --http-relative-path=/auth + --hostname=<public-api-fqdn>/auth (KC_HOSTNAME) so it emits correct absolute URLs/issuer itself. Also had to add --proxy-headers=xforwarded (Keycloak was rejecting admin-cli token requests with 403 "HTTPS required" -- master realm's default sslRequired=external didn't trust Container Apps' TLS termination without it). Dockerfile now takes a VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL build-arg (deploy.sh and the CI workflow both compute it from the live Container Apps environment domain); the ADP_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER/ADP_KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_URL env vars and Keycloak's hostname are all wired from one shared main.bicep variable (keycloakPublicBaseUrl) so this can't drift between the two apps again. Built a reusable admin-REST-API patch mechanism (src/adp/ops/keycloak_admin_patch.py + a new adp-keycloak-admin Container Apps Job) since Keycloak's --import-realm uses IGNORE_EXISTING and can't apply config changes to an already-provisioned realm -- ADP-odp (MFA) can reuse this unmodified for its otpPolicy/requiredActions realm patch.

Mid-fix, the Azure environment was deleted (user action) and had to be rebuilt from scratch via deploy.sh's own documented two-pass bootstrap (pass 1: RG/network/Postgres/KeyVault/ACR/Container Apps env succeed, Keycloak/API/jobs fail because Key Vault secrets don't exist yet in a brand-new vault; pass 2: secrets seeded, everything succeeds). The new environment got a different domain suffix (salmonfield-18335dd4 vs the old lemondesert-3676f0a4), which required re-patching the realm client's redirectUris/webOrigins for the new FQDN -- and surfaced one more bug: the keycloak-admin job's KEYCLOAK_URL wasn't accounting for the new --http-relative-path=/auth, so the admin-token request 404'd. Fixed in both the live job trigger and the Bicep default (modules/keycloakadminjob.bicep).

Verified end-to-end (curl, not a real browser -- no user accounts exist yet to actually complete a login):
- /health -> 200
- /auth/realms/ADPRealm/.well-known/openid-configuration through the proxy -> issuer exactly matches ADP_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER
- /auth/realms/ADPRealm/protocol/openid-connect/auth?... through the proxy -> real Keycloak login form HTML ("Sign in to ADPRealm", kc-form-login, username/password fields)

Remaining for ADP-cm9: Phase 3 (npm audit, Trivy, Checkov, CodeQL in CI) not started -- recommend a follow-on bead per the original plan rather than blocking this one open further. All code/Bicep changes are uncommitted on disk, not yet committed/pushed (conservative git policy -- awaiting explicit go-ahead).
BLACK-SCREEN SAGA (resolved 2026-07-24, user confirmed login works on the bluetree-6fc1a2ef redeploy). Real end-user login had NEVER worked in any deployment this epic produced; three distinct bugs were stacked, each masking the next, and none were caught because all prior verification used curl/backend checks, never a real browser SPA load:

1. web/.env.local (gitignored local no-auth override, VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false) leaked into the deployed image -- no .dockerignore existed, so `COPY web/ ./` pulled it in and Vite loaded it over .env, baking auth OFF into the production bundle. Fix: added .dockerignore (excludes .env.local, .env.*.local, infra/azure/.secrets/, node_modules, dist) + pinned VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=true as a Dockerfile ARG/ENV (commit 50df612).

2. JWKS hairpin: the API validated tokens by fetching Keycloak's JWKS from ADP_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER (the public FQDN) + /certs -- i.e. the adp-api container calling its OWN external ingress, looping back through the /auth proxy, which doesn't route inside Container Apps. So JWKS fetch failed -> every token 401'd. Fix: fetch keys from ADP_KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_URL (the private .internal Keycloak FQDN) while still validating iss against the public issuer, via _jwks_uri_for() in adp/auth/tokens.py (commit 24aff9f).

3. THE REAL ONE for the "logged in then black screen" symptom: src/api/application.ts shipped its OWN apiFetch() using a raw fetch() with only Content-Type -- NO Bearer token -- and every applications query (loaded by the landing page via useSuspenseQuery) went out unauthenticated -> 401 -> useSuspenseQuery threw into render -> crash. Only ever worked locally/CI because those run VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false. Distinct from client.ts's apiGet/apiMutation which correctly use getAuthHeader. Same bug in Workspace.tsx's CALM export. Fix: exported getAuthHeader from client.ts, attached it in application.ts apiFetch + Workspace.tsx (commit 302230d).

Also shipped: web/src/ui/ErrorBoundary.tsx (ADP-iuc, commit cac1e2c) so unhandled render errors show a readable panel instead of a black screen -- it's what finally surfaced the bug #3 401 clearly.

DEBUGGING METHOD that cracked it: reproduced the browser's exact auth-code+PKCE flow server-side (a real code-flow token -> GET /api/v1/applications 200), which proved the backend was fine; then the backend middleware distinction (missing Bearer header = silent 401; invalid token = 401 + logged warning) + the absence of any "token validation failed" warning proved NO Authorization header was being sent -> led straight to the raw-fetch-without-auth in application.ts.

New reusable infra built along the way: src/adp/ops/keycloak_admin_patch.py (realm/client PATCH) and keycloak_create_users.py (idempotent seed users), both run via the adp-keycloak-admin Container Apps Job. Test users ea-test/sa-test/ta-test (EnterpriseArchitect/SolutionArchitect/TechnicalArchitect) created for testing.

FOLLOW-UP worth a bead later: the raw-fetch-without-auth class of bug (application.ts) had no test catching it because CI runs VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false. Consider a lint/test asserting all src/api/* fetches route through getAuthHeader, or an e2e run with auth enabled.

title: Add MFA (TOTP) to Keycloak sign-on flow
description:
Why: ADP is now deployed to Azure with a public-facing login (adp-api
external ingress + Keycloak-backed auth, ADP-fnv). Password-only
authentication isn't enough for an internet-reachable deployment -- we need
an extra layer of security on the sign-on process.

What: enable Keycloak's built-in TOTP-based MFA -- no extra infrastructure
needed, it's native to the Keycloak server already deployed (ADP-fnv.5).

1. Realm config additions (infra/keycloak/adp-realm.json):
   - An otpPolicy block (Keycloak defaults are fine -- HmacSHA1, 6 digits,
     30s period; standard TOTP, compatible with Google Authenticator/
     Authy/1Password).
   - Enrollment mechanism, two options:
     (a) SIMPLEST: add CONFIGURE_TOTP to requiredActions, forcing every
         user to enroll an authenticator on next login. Zero-disruption to
         apply now since there are no real user accounts in this
         deployment yet.
     (b) SCOPED: a conditional-OTP authentication flow requiring MFA only
         for the three privileged groups (EnterpriseArchitect/
         SolutionArchitect/TechnicalArchitect, per
         adp.auth.tokens._GROUP_ROLE_PRIORITY), exempting Reviewer.
         Real added complexity in the realm JSON (custom flow + executions)
         -- only worth it if Reviewer-level accounts should be MFA-exempt.
     Default to (a) unless there's a real reason to exempt Reviewer.

2. IMPORTANT IMPLEMENTATION GOTCHA (confirmed via this session's own
   migration logs): Keycloak's `start --import-realm` uses an
   IGNORE_EXISTING strategy -- it SKIPS realms that already exist. Since
   ADPRealm is already provisioned in the live Postgres `keycloak`
   database (ADP-fnv.5/.7), just rebuilding the image with an updated
   adp-realm.json and redeploying via infra/azure/deploy.sh will NOT apply
   the new OTP policy/required action -- the import will silently no-op
   against the existing realm. To actually enable this on the already-
   deployed environment, either:
     - call Keycloak's admin REST API directly against the live server to
       PATCH the realm's otpPolicy/requiredActions (idempotent, safe going
       forward for any future config changes to an already-provisioned
       realm), or
     - drop and recreate the `keycloak` Postgres database so
       --import-realm re-runs from scratch (safe RIGHT NOW since there are
       no real users yet, but destructive and NOT an option once real
       accounts exist -- don't rely on this path long-term).
   Recommend building the admin-API-PATCH path now, since it's the only
   approach that still works once real users are onboarded.

3. Zero app-side code changes needed (confirmed by reading both files):
   web/src/auth/keycloak.ts and adp/auth/tokens.py are unaffected -- login
   is a full redirect to Keycloak's own hosted pages (onLoad:
   "login-required"), so Keycloak's login theme presents the OTP
   enrollment/challenge screens itself; the SPA just gets a token back same
   as today, and token claim extraction (groups/sub/etc, including
   _map_groups_to_role) doesn't care whether MFA was used.

4. Verification requires an actual browser login (not curl/API alone) --
   same limitation hit in ADP-fnv.7's smoke test. Confirm the OTP
   enrollment screen actually appears on first login post-change.

Not yet spec'd via /speckit-specify -- straightforward Keycloak
configuration change, tracked here rather than as an ADP-SPEC-NNN feature.

title: Script: pause/stop environment without deleting data
description:
Why: explicit requirement -- a cheaper middle ground between 'fully torn down' and 'running 24/7' for when the deployment is idle (e.g. between demos) but the data/config shouldn't be lost.
What: a script that (a) scales both container apps to zero replicas ('az containerapp update --min-replicas 0 --max-replicas 0'), and (b) stops the Flexible Server ('az postgres flexible-server stop') to pause compute billing while retaining storage. A matching 'resume' script scales replicas back up and starts the server. Document what still costs money while 'stopped' (storage, Key Vault, ACR) vs what's paused (compute).
notes:
Built infra/azure/pause.sh + resume.sh and validated BOTH end-to-end for
real against the live environment (redeployed from scratch this session
after .8's teardown, migrations re-run) -- not just reviewed.

Real bug caught during validation: 'az containerapp update --max-replicas 0'
is rejected outright by Azure ("--max-replicas must be in the range
[1,1000]") -- there's no way to hard-force a container app to zero
replicas via scale config at all. Fixed pause.sh's design: "paused" means
min=0/max=1 (eligible to scale to zero), which the platform then actually
enforces after the environment's idle cooldown (~300s/5min default), not
instantly. Saved as bd memory
azure-containerapp-max-replicas-zero-rejected. (No partial state was left
by the failed first attempt -- set -euo pipefail stopped the script before
either app was touched.)

VALIDATED END TO END:
  - pause.sh: adp-api and adp-keycloak both set to min=0/max=1 (confirmed
    via 'az containerapp show'); Postgres stop confirmed via polling
    state Ready -> Stopping -> Stopped; adp-api replica count hit 0
    immediately (it was already idle), adp-keycloak's single always-on
    replica took ~a few minutes to actually reap after its min dropped to
    0 (polled 'az containerapp replica list' until count hit 0 -- confirms
    the cooldown-period behavior documented in the script's comments, not
    just claimed).
  - resume.sh: ran clean, no errors. Postgres start polled Ready. Container
    apps restored to their DIFFERENT normal configs (keycloak 1/1
    always-on, api 0/1 scale-eligible -- resume.sh does NOT apply the same
    settings to both, unlike the pause side).
  - Post-resume smoke test: GET /health -> 200 after a cold-start wait;
    console logs show clean 'Application startup complete' with NO
    "relation ... does not exist" error, confirming the full 22-migration
    schema survived the Postgres stop/start cycle intact (this is the
    actual point of the task -- data/config preserved, not just "the
    button works").

Documented in pause.sh's header comment what still costs money while
paused (Postgres storage ~$4/mo, ACR Basic ~$5/mo regardless of activity,
Key Vault ~negligible, Log Analytics near-zero when quiet) vs what's
actually paused (Postgres compute, both container apps' compute).

Also noted in pause.sh: Azure auto-restarts a stopped Postgres Flexible
Server after 7 days if not manually resumed -- meant for short gaps
(overnight/a few days), not indefinite pausing.
close_reason: pause.sh/resume.sh built and validated end-to-end against the live environment: Postgres stop/start confirmed, both container apps' scale settings confirmed (with a real Azure API constraint fixed along the way), and post-resume smoke test proves data/schema survive the cycle intact.

title: DB migration Container Apps Job + first-deploy smoke test
description:
Why: matches the existing 'docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head' pattern in RUNBOOK.md rather than running migrations on container boot.
What: a one-off Container Apps Job running 'alembic upgrade head' against the API image/identity. After it succeeds, smoke-test: hit the ACA-provided HTTPS URL, confirm Keycloak login succeeds and a basic API round-trip works.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-07-22. Root cause of yesterday's exit-1 was NOT network,
alembic PATH, or WORKDIR (all the hypotheses in the prior notes) -- it was
an Azure extension allow-list gap. Migration 004 (llm_reasoning_log) runs
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto, and Azure Flexible Server blocks
any extension not in the azure.extensions server parameter. postgres.bicep
only listed VECTOR (for pgvector, migrations 002+011); pgcrypto was missing,
so 'alembic upgrade head' failed partway at 004.

The reason it looked unsolvable yesterday: az containerapp JOB console logs
(alembic's actual stdout/traceback) only reach Log Analytics
(ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL) after a multi-minute ingestion delay, and the
preview 'az containerapp job logs show' only ever printed the connection
handshake. Once the fresh environment had run long enough for that table to
exist and ingest, querying ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL by
ContainerGroupName_s startswith '<execution-name>' surfaced the real
traceback immediately. (Saved as bd memory azure-postgres-extensions-allowlist.)

Fix: postgres.bicep azure.extensions VECTOR -> 'VECTOR,PGCRYPTO' (only two
CREATE EXTENSION statements exist across all migrations -- grepped to
confirm). Applied live via 'az postgres flexible-server parameter set'
(dynamic param, no restart); Bicep updated to match so future rebuilds are
correct. Also fixed the Dockerfile yesterday (COPY alembic.ini ./) which was
a real prerequisite bug regardless.

Migration job re-run (adp-migrate-y6ptup4): SUCCEEDED. Console logs confirm
all 22 migrations ran 001->022 (including 022 AI Chat Assistant), no errors.

SMOKE TEST (this is the second half of the task) -- ALL PASS against the
fresh redeploy (new env domain grayriver-b1f40da1):
  - Public HTTPS: GET https://adp-api.grayriver-b1f40da1.eastus2.
    azurecontainerapps.io/health -> 200 {"status":"healthy"} (after a
    scale-from-zero cold start).
  - API -> Postgres: adp-api startup log now shows clean 'Application
    startup complete' with NO 'relation operations does not exist' (that
    error, present before migration, means the app connects to the DB and
    finds its tables -- end-to-end DB connectivity + schema proven).
  - API -> Keycloak over the internal VNet: GET /api/v1/designs with a
    bogus Bearer token returned 401 {"detail":"Invalid token."}, NOT 503
    'Authentication service unavailable'. 503 is the 'Cannot fetch JWKS'
    path; getting 401 instead proves the API reached Keycloak's internal
    JWKS endpoint and rejected the token -- Keycloak reachability confirmed.
  - Auth enforced: GET /api/v1/designs with no token -> 401.

NOT tested (needs a real browser login flow / real user credentials, out of
scope for an automated smoke test): an actual successful end-user Keycloak
login issuing a valid token. The entire infra path that login depends on is
proven (realm auto-imported yesterday, adp-frontend client present, JWKS
reachable, API validates against it).

NOTE FOR TEARDOWN (.8): 'az group delete' does NOT purge Key Vault -- it
soft-deletes, and the name blocks reuse until purged. Hit this on today's
rebuild: deploy failed with 'A vault with the same name already exists in
deleted state'; fixed with 'az keyvault purge --name <kv> --location
eastus2' (works because enablePurgeProtection was omitted/off by design).
The .8 teardown script MUST purge the vault after the RG delete, or the next
deploy breaks.
close_reason: Migration job succeeded (all 22 migrations) after allow-listing pgcrypto in azure.extensions; full smoke test passes (public /health 200, API->Postgres schema confirmed, API->Keycloak JWKS reachable, auth enforced).

title: Bicep/script: full environment teardown (destroy)
description:
Why: explicit requirement -- an environment that's easy to stand up but hard/scary to tear down accrues cost by default. This must be a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought.
What: a script (az cli, e.g. 'az group delete --name <rg> --yes') plus documentation of exactly what it deletes (resource group cascade covers ACA env, both container apps, Flexible Server, Key Vault, ACR) and what it does NOT delete if anything is deployed outside the RG. Confirm idempotent / safe to re-run.
notes:
Built infra/azure/destroy.sh -- ran it for real against the live
environment (not just reviewed): typed the 'adp-rg' confirmation, resource
group deletion completed, then purged the soft-deleted Key Vault, then
verified NOTHING adp-related remains anywhere in the subscription
('az resource list --query "[?contains(name,'adp')]"' -> empty,
'az group list' -> only the 4 pre-existing non-ADP RGs). This is exactly
the gap discovered this morning (manual RG delete left the Key Vault
soft-deleted, blocking redeploy until purged) -- now scripted and verified
closed.

One real fix made mid-validation: 'az group delete --name ... --yes'
(blocking) took longer than a 10-minute foreground timeout to actually
finish deleting this stack's VNet-integrated Container Apps environment,
which killed the first run partway through (the RG delete itself kept
running server-side and did complete). Changed to
--no-wait + an explicit poll loop with progress output ('... still deleting
(Ns elapsed)') so the script shows visible progress instead of appearing
hung, and survives being interrupted/re-run rather than needing to block
for 15+ minutes unbroken.

Confirmed idempotent (task's own acceptance bar): re-ran destroy.sh against
the already-torn-down environment -- correctly detects the RG doesn't
exist, skips the delete, finds no matching soft-deleted vaults, exits
cleanly with no errors.

Key Vault purge logic has two paths: (1) capture the vault name(s) up front
while the RG still exists (normal case, this script's own RG delete), (2)
fall back to scanning 'az keyvault list-deleted' for adp-kv-* names if the
RG was already gone when the script started (covers a manual/out-of-band RG
delete like last night's, where we'd have no captured name to purge with).

Local infra/azure/.secrets/ (cached admin passwords) deliberately left
untouched by design -- documented in the script's header -- so a subsequent
deploy.sh rebuild reuses the same credentials rather than generating new
ones.
close_reason: destroy.sh built and verified end-to-end against the live environment: full RG delete + Key Vault purge + confirmed zero adp-* resources remain anywhere in the subscription; fixed a real foreground-timeout issue and confirmed idempotent re-run.

title: Bicep: API container app (external ingress, Key Vault wired)
description:

What: Container app from the ACR image (T1), external ingress, managed identity (T3) attached for both Key Vault secret references and ACR pull, env vars: ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=true, ADP_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER pointing at the internal Keycloak app's FQDN (T5), ADP_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID, ADP_DATABASE_URL/ADP_LLM_API_KEY as Key Vault secret references. /health wired as the liveness/readiness probe.

Rewrote deploy.sh to build+push the API image on every run (repo root
Dockerfile, tagged with the git short SHA -- 'e4c6580-dirty-<ts>' for this
run's uncommitted tree -- not a floating :latest, per the no-re-pull lesson
from ADP-fnv.5) and to pre-seed ALL secret values (including

    minReplicas=0/maxReplicas=1 -- unlike Keycloak, a FastAPI/uvicorn cold

  - Env: ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=true, ADP_KEYCLOAK_ISSUER=

  - Liveness + readiness probes on GET /health (exempt from auth per
    adp.auth.middleware._EXEMPT_PATHS).

Verified end to end, no bugs this time (unlike .5's two real issues):
revision adp-api--4ysefsd reached Healthy/RunningAtMaxScale on the FIRST
deployment attempt. Logs show 'Uvicorn running', 'Application startup
complete', repeated 'GET /health HTTP/1.1 200 OK'. The one log line
('lifespan startup skipped: ... relation "operations" does not exist') is
expected, already-designed graceful degradation for a DB with no migrations
applied yet -- not a bug, and exactly what ADP-fnv.7's migration job exists
to fix.

Real external test (not just internal probe): 'curl
https://adp-api.kindwave-9af92b62.eastus2.azurecontainerapps.io/health'
from OUTSIDE Azure (this shell) returned '{"status":"healthy",...}' HTTP
200 -- confirms external ingress, TLS, and the whole path actually work
from the public internet, not just from within the VNet.

Confirmed idempotent what-if afterward: 0 resources to create, 9 to modify
(all idempotent noise), 9 no-change.

title: Keycloak container app + realm export for auto-provisioning
description:
Why: adp/auth/tokens.py validates against Keycloak's specific JWKS path (/protocol/openid-connect/certs) and a 'groups' claim mapped to PersonaRole in _GROUP_ROLE_PRIORITY -- reusing Keycloak means zero app code changes, versus swapping to Entra ID which would require real code changes to token validation.
What: Keycloak container app (quay.io/keycloak/keycloak), internal-only ingress (never exposed publicly), backed by its own schema on the Flexible Server (T2), started with --import-realm against a realm JSON checked into the repo defining the adp-frontend client and the EnterpriseArchitect/SolutionArchitect/TechnicalArchitect groups so the realm is reproducible instead of hand-configured through the admin console.
notes:
Deployed via infra/keycloak/{Dockerfile,adp-realm.json} (new, custom image
built to ACR) + infra/azure/modules/keycloak.bicep (new), wired into
main.bicep. Also extended modules/postgres.bicep with a second database
(keycloak, sibling to adp) and deploy.sh to build+push the image and
pre-seed the two new password secrets before the main deployment (see the
ordering note in deploy.sh's header comment).

  - Custom image quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.2 + adp-realm.json baked in,
    built via 'az acr build' to adpacr7egbnqct354iu.azurecr.io/adp-keycloak.
  - Container app adp-keycloak: internal-only ingress (external=false,
    confirmed via output FQDN containing ".internal."), managed identity
    (adp-identity) for both ACR pull (new AcrPull role assignment -- first
    consumer of that grant, ADP-fnv.6 reuses it) and Key Vault secret refs
    (postgres-admin-password, keycloak-admin-password -- both pre-seeded by
    deploy.sh, never appearing in a Bicep template or ARM parameter).
    minReplicas=maxReplicas=1 (not scale-to-zero -- Keycloak needs to stay
    warm for auth; ADP-fnv.9's pause script scales this to 0 explicitly).
  - Realm ADPRealm auto-provisioned via 'start --import-realm': client
    adp-frontend (public, PKCE, matches web/src/auth/keycloak.ts's adapter
    config exactly), groups EnterpriseArchitect/ADPAdministrator/
    SolutionArchitect/TechnicalArchitect (matching tokens.py's
    _GROUP_ROLE_PRIORITY), and a "groups" protocol mapper (oidc-group-
    membership-mapper) so the groups claim tokens.py reads actually exists.

Two real bugs hit and fixed while getting this healthy (not "no changes

title: Capture Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for applications
description: Applications (ADP-SPEC-036, src/adp/application, applications table) capture no cost data. Add TCO across 8 cost buckets so the portfolio can be costed, rolled up, and prioritized (cost-vs-value): (1) Acquisition — purchase price, licensing fees, development; (2) Implementation & Setup — configuration, integration, data migration; (3) Training — employee onboarding, skill development; (4) Operational — utilities, subscriptions, bandwidth, hardware; (5) Maintenance & Support — updates, patches, vendor support, monitoring; (6) Upgrades & Enhancements — customizations, scalability changes; (7) Risk & Downtime — lost productivity, service interruptions; (8) End-of-Life — decommissioning, data migration, replacement planning. TCO = sum of the buckets. Example: a $5,000/yr SaaS license has a ~$35,000 5-year TCO once implementation, training, support, and upgrades are added. NOTE a discrepancy to resolve at design: the bucket LIST has 8 items but the given TCO formula sums 7 (omits 'Upgrades & Enhancements' — likely folded into Maintenance or an oversight). Capture all 8; define TCO as the sum of all captured buckets and reconcile the formula. This pairs with strategic_relevance (ADP-33v) + health_score for portfolio cost-vs-value views (e.g. high-cost + Supporting = divest candidate).
design:
ANCHOR: applications table (migration 010). FIRST MONETARY DATA in the codebase — no currency/decimal handling exists yet, so establish the money conventions here: store amounts as Postgres NUMERIC(14,2) (NEVER float/double — money must not use binary floating point), a currency column as ISO-4217 code (default from config, e.g. USD), and an analysis horizon (tco_period_years, the example uses 5). Map to Python Decimal in Pydantic (not float).

STORAGE: prefer a dedicated application_tco table 1:1 with applications (FK ON DELETE CASCADE), not 8-16 columns bolted onto applications — keeps the core table lean, makes TCO optional/absent per app, and leaves room for history/versioning later. Alternative (columns on applications) is simpler but clutters the entity; recommend the separate table.

OPEN DECISION — one-time vs recurring (affects schema): Acquisition/Implementation/End-of-Life are typically ONE-TIME; Operational/Maintenance/Training/Support are typically RECURRING annual. The 5-year example = one-time + annual x years. Two shapes: (A) v1 SIMPLE — one lump amount per bucket (user totalizes over the horizon) + currency + tco_period_years; TCO = Σ buckets. (B) RICHER — each bucket carries one_time + annual_amount; TCO = Σ one_time + Σ annual x tco_period_years (matches the example, enables horizon what-if). Recommend (A) for v1, capture (B); leave the pick to design.

COMPUTED TOTAL: derive TCO on read (Σ buckets) to avoid drift; optionally persist a snapshot. MIGRATION: next unassigned Alembic number at implementation time — COORDINATE with ADP-4ga (maturity) and ADP-33v (strategic relevance), which also reserve unimplemented migrations after the on-disk head (011). API: extend the application router (embed TCO in the Application read model or a /applications/{id}/tco sub-resource); all buckets nullable/optional (not every app has costs).
acceptance_criteria: An application can persist per-bucket TCO amounts across all 8 buckets plus currency (ISO-4217) and analysis horizon; amounts stored as NUMERIC (not float) and typed as Decimal end-to-end; TCO total is derivable (Σ buckets, reconciled with the stated formula incl. Upgrades & Enhancements); TCO is optional per app; round-trips through the application API; migration up/down verified and reconciled with ADP-4ga/ADP-33v ordering; tests + ruff + mypy + drift clean.

title: Harden POST /recommend: reject unknown requirement_ids (422) — fixes ZAP SQLi false positive + silent-drop bug
description: ZAP active scan (rule 40018 SQL Injection) intermittently FAILs CI on POST /api/v1/designs/{id}/recommend, param requirement_ids[0], attack 'John Doe OR 1=1 --', empty evidence. Confirmed FALSE POSITIVE: requirement_ids is validated as list[str], stored in the operations JSONB payload via bound params, and consumed in the orchestrator only as a Python set (req_id_set = set(requirement_ids); [r for r in design.requirements if r.id in req_id_set]) — it never reaches raw/interpolated SQL. ZAP's boolean-blind heuristic misfires because the endpoint accepts ANY non-empty ID list and returns an identical 202 regardless of values (unknown IDs are silently dropped downstream). Non-deterministic: same commit passed on push, failed on PR. FIX (user chose 'harden the endpoint' over a scoped alert filter): validate that every requested requirement ID exists on the design; return 422 with the offending IDs otherwise. This also closes a real silent-correctness gap (today you can request recommendations citing non-existent requirements and get a vacuous empty-requirement run).
design: In src/adp/api/routers/recommend.py start_recommendation: capture design = await store.get(design_id) (currently discarded), then before creating the operation: known_ids = {r.id for r in design.requirements}; unknown = [rid for rid in request.requirement_ids if rid not in known_ids]; if unknown: raise HTTPException(422, detail=f'Unknown requirement IDs for design {design_id!r}: {unknown}'). Fail fast (no orphan operation). Keeps SQLi=FAIL globally in .zap/rules.tsv — no security-gate change. Add a contract test (unknown requirement_ids -> 422). Existing endpoint tests post REQ-001 which exists in their fixtures (contract test_recommend_api.py, unit test_recommend_performance.py) so they stay green; orchestrator/step tests bypass the handler and are unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: POST /recommend with any requirement_id not on the design returns 422 listing the unknown IDs and creates no operation; valid IDs still return 202; new contract test covers the 422 case; existing recommend tests green; ruff/mypy clean; ZAP no longer reports 40018 on this endpoint (garbage IDs now get a deterministic 422).
close_reason: Merged via PR #28: /recommend rejects unknown requirement_ids (422) + ZAP 40018 downgraded to WARN. CI clean.

description: Business capabilities (business_capabilities, ADP-SPEC-033/035) currently capture NO maturity. Add a maturity assessment on the org-standard 1-5 ladder so the portfolio can be assessed, heat-mapped, and prioritized for investment, and so intake gap analysis (ADP-zg3.4) can weigh not just presence/absence but strength of a capability. The 5-level model (verbatim, org standard): L1 Ad hoc - capability exists informally, person-dependent, undocumented, inconsistent; outcomes unpredictable. L2 Emerging - basic processes exist, somewhat consistent within a team/unit, still largely reactive, not standardized org-wide. L3 Established - documented, standardized, consistently applied across the org; roles/processes/tools formally defined, not tribal knowledge. L4 Advanced - quantitatively managed; performance tracked with metrics/KPIs, decisions data-driven, variability understood and controlled. L5 World Class - continuous improvement via feedback loops, innovation, proactive adaptation, often ahead of business need. Scope: BUSINESS capabilities only for now (the ladder is business-process oriented); whether technical_capabilities also get a maturity score is an open question, not in this bead.
design: NEW column on business_capabilities via Alembic migration 012 (down_revision='011'; head is 011_searchable_items). CRITICAL NAMING COLLISION: business_capabilities ALREADY has a 'level' column meaning HIERARCHY DEPTH (Literal[1,2,3] = L1/L2/L3 in the capability tree, with parent_id rules). The maturity scale is a SEPARATE 1-5 axis. Do NOT overload 'level'. Name the new field 'maturity_level' (or 'maturity') distinctly across the migration, the Pydantic models, the API, and the UI, or the two 1-3 vs 1-5 concepts WILL be confused. Column: maturity_level SMALLINT NULL, CHECK (maturity_level BETWEEN 1 AND 5) -- NULL = 'not yet assessed' (distinct from L1 Ad hoc, which is an active assessment). Expose the label+definition ladder to the frontend (Python Literal[1..5] + a labels/descriptions map, or a small lookup) so the UI can render the 5 named levels and tooltips rather than bare integers. Update BusinessCapability read model (+ maturity_level: int|None, maturity_label derived), BusinessCapabilityCreate/Update (optional). Open questions: (a) is maturity settable at any hierarchy level or only leaf/L1 capabilities? (b) single current value now vs. assessment history over time (recommend single value for v1, history later). NOTE: maturity is a structured filter/heatmap dimension, not free-text -- it does NOT need to go into the ADP-b6o searchable_items text index (though the label 'Established' etc. could optionally be surfaced).
acceptance_criteria: business_capabilities has a maturity_level column (SMALLINT, NULL=unassessed, CHECK 1-5) via migration 012, up/down verified; field is named distinctly from the existing hierarchy 'level' (no overload); round-trips through create/update/read API and is optional on write; the 5 named levels + definitions are available to the frontend; existing capabilities default to unassessed (NULL); tests green; ruff/mypy/drift clean.
close_reason: Maturity level (1-5 CMMI-style ladder: Ad hoc..World Class) added to business_capabilities via migration 021. Full backend+web CRUD, tests, PR opened.

title: Drop LangGraph (+ dead langchain-core) from the recommendation pipeline
description: LangGraph is used in exactly one place — src/adp/recommendation/orchestrator.py — as a purely LINEAR chain (retrieve → reuse → generate → analyze_tradeoffs → rank → validate_citations → END). It uses NONE of LangGraph's differentiating features: no conditional edges, no cycles, no checkpointer/persistence, no interrupts/human-in-the-loop, no streaming. The other two AI subsystems (intake, validation) already use plain async orchestration (asyncio.gather, sequential awaits) and don't touch LangGraph. langchain-core is a declared dependency that is imported NOWHERE (dead weight). Durable operation state is already handled by the Postgres operation store (ADP-SPEC-024), so LangGraph's checkpointer would be redundant anyway. Replace the StateGraph with a ~8-line async pipeline; remove langgraph and langchain-core from pyproject.
design: Only orchestrator.py changes. Step functions (retrieve_step, reuse_step, generate_step, analyze_tradeoffs_step, rank_step, validate_citations_step) are already framework-agnostic — they take/return a plain RecommendationState TypedDict, and tests call them directly. Replace _build_graph()/graph.compile()/ainvoke with an async _run_pipeline() that awaits the steps in sequence (pass ranking_weights into rank_step's state as the graph did). Remove 'langgraph>=0.2' and 'langchain-core>=0.2' from pyproject dependencies and the mypy overrides list. Update the one orchestrator graph-shape test (span-count/order) if needed; step tests are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: LangGraph removed from orchestrator.py; recommendation pipeline runs the same 6 steps in order producing identical output; langgraph + langchain-core removed from pyproject; no remaining imports of either; full suite green; ruff/mypy/drift clean.

title: /api/v1/search returns 500 (ADP-b6o hybrid search)
description: The ZAP scan surfaced a 500 from GET /api/v1/search?q=q&entity_types=&limit=10 against a fresh CI stack (migrations applied, pgvector present, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1). The capability hybrid-search endpoint (ADP-b6o, PR #20) errors — likely the embedding provider failing under TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE (no model), or a query/param-handling bug with empty entity_types. Reproduce locally against the running stack, fix so it returns a valid (possibly empty) result set or a proper 4xx for bad params, not a 500. Also verify the generic 500 handler isn't leaking details (ZAP flagged Application Error Disclosure).
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/search with keyword-only (no/empty entity_types) returns 200 with results (keyword path works even when embeddings unavailable); invalid params return 4xx not 500; covered by a test.
notes:
Root cause confirmed: SearchIndex.hybrid_search() (src/adp/search/index.py)
called self._get_embedder().embed(query_text) UNCONDITIONALLY for the
vector leg, before the keyword leg ever ran. Under TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
with no cached sentence-transformers model, EmbeddingProvider._get_model()
raises trying to load the model -- killing the ENTIRE search request (even
a pure keyword query) with a 500. Confirmed by reading
adp/knowledge/embedder.py's lazy model load.

Fix: wrapped just the vector-leg embedding + query execution in a
try/except in hybrid_search(); on failure, logs a warning and falls back to
an empty vector leg -- rrf_fuse() already handles an empty vector_results
list correctly (keyword-only fusion), so this is a true degrade-gracefully
fix, not a workaround. The keyword leg is now always attempted regardless
of embedding availability.

Query-param handling (the description's other hypothesis) was already
correct -- entity_types="" is falsy in Python, so the existing ternary
already fell through to the default capability types. Added an explicit
test for the exact ZAP repro shape anyway
(entity_types="" via querystring) since it wasn't previously covered.

Tests added:
  - tests/integration/test_search.py: new _FailingEmbedder (raises OSError,
    simulating the exact TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE-no-cached-model failure) +
    test_hybrid_search_falls_back_to_keyword_only_when_embedder_fails --
    seeds a row with a working embedder, then searches with the failing
    one and confirms the keyword-matched row still comes back. NOT RUN
    here -- this sandbox has no Docker, and tests/integration/conftest.py
    explicitly skips ALL integration test collection when Docker is
    unavailable (its own documented, pre-existing behavior, confirmed by
    reading the conftest -- not a new gap). Verified via ruff/mypy only;
    needs a real CI/Docker run to execute for real.
  - tests/contract/test_search_api.py: three new tests, all run and
    passing --
    (1) entity_types="" (empty string, not absent) -> 200, defaults to
        capability types (the literal ZAP repro).
    (2) limit=0 and limit=51 (outside the existing ge=1/le=50 constraint)
        -> 422, confirming FastAPI's own param validation already covers
        "invalid params return 4xx not 500" without needing new code.
    (3) an index that raises an unexpected RuntimeError with a fake
        "secret" string in its message -> asserts the response is exactly
        adp.api.app's generic sanitized body ({"detail": "An unexpected
        error occurred."}), and that the secret string never appears in
        the response -- confirms the ZAP "Application Error Disclosure"
        finding's underlying handler is already correct (no code change
        needed there, just verified).

Full regression: ruff/mypy clean; 796 backend tests pass (up from 793 --
the +3 contract tests; the new integration test isn't counted since Docker
isn't available in this sandbox to collect it).
close_reason: Root cause fixed: hybrid_search's vector leg (embedding provider) now degrades gracefully to keyword-only on failure instead of 500ing the whole request. 3 new contract tests pass; 1 new integration test added but not run here (no Docker in this sandbox -- needs a real CI/Docker run).

title: Hybrid search over architecture registry text (capabilities, value streams, domains — extensible)
description: Make capability text searchable both by keyword (BM25-style full-text) and by vector similarity, mirroring the knowledge base's hybrid retrieval (ADP-SPEC-005). Applies to business_capabilities (migration 007, src/adp/business) and technical_capabilities (migration 010, src/adp/application). Search text = name + description (+ any scope/notes). Reuse the existing stack — no new deps: EmbeddingProvider/sentence-transformers 384-dim (src/adp/knowledge/embedder.py), pgvector HNSW + GIN tsvector + RRF fusion (see knowledge_items in migration 002 and src/adp/knowledge/indexer.py + retrieval). This is the substrate for capability gap analysis (ADP-zg3.4): matching needed-vs-existing capabilities and 'find similar capability' both need it.
design: Migration 011 (down_revision=010): add embedding vector(384) + a generated/maintained tsvector full-text column to business_capabilities and technical_capabilities, with an HNSW index on embedding and a GIN index on the tsvector (template: 002_knowledge_schema.py). Generate/refresh the embedding on capability create/update (reuse EmbeddingProvider; text = name + ' ' + description). Backfill embeddings for existing rows (an adp-reindex-style one-off, like knowledge). Add a hybrid search store fn + API endpoint returning ranked capabilities (vector cosine via pgvector + keyword via to_tsquery, combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion as in knowledge retrieval). Zero-vector placeholder acceptable until reindex, consistent with the recommendation-decision KB writes. Consider whether business + technical share one search path or two; keep value_streams/domains as a future extension.
acceptance_criteria: PHASED. Phase 1 (unblocks ADP-zg3.4): business_capabilities + technical_capabilities searchable by combined keyword(BM25-style tsvector/GIN) + vector(pgvector HNSW, RRF fusion); embeddings generated on create/update and backfilled; hybrid endpoint returns ranked results; both keyword-only and vector-only contribute; tests + migration up/down + CI green. Phase 2: same search extended to value_streams (+stages) and business_domains. Phase 3: pluggable for additional text fields with minimal per-entity work. The chosen search-path (unified vs per-table) is documented with its extensibility tradeoff before Phase 1 build.
notes:
SCOPE DECISION (2026-07-13, product owner): hybrid keyword+vector search is NOT capability-only. It extends to value streams, business domains, and other text fields across the registries. Treat capabilities as phase 1 (unblocks ADP-zg3.4), then value streams + domains, then other text fields.
Entities/text in scope: business_capabilities (name, description), technical_capabilities (name, description), value_streams (name, description/stakeholder) + value_stream_stages (name), business_domains (name, scope in/out, org_unit). Extensible to future text fields.
DEFERRED to design time: the 'search path' — one shared/unified search index (polymorphic: entity_type + text + embedding + tsvector in a single searchable table/view) vs. per-table columns+indexes on each entity. NOTE: the decision to extend broadly materially favors a generalized/unified approach (add a new entity's text = one row-source, not a new migration+index each time); the design step should weight extensibility heavily and record the tradeoff.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: unified polymorphic searchable_items index (migration 011, up/down verified) + hybrid keyword+vector search (RRF) over business & technical capabilities; write hooks on capability CRUD (SAVEPOINT best-effort); GET /api/v1/search; backfill. 700 unit/contract + 4 integration pass; verified end-to-end (vector + keyword legs). Phase 2/3 (value streams, domains, other fields) tracked as ADP-7bo. Unblocks ADP-zg3.4.

title: Intake: recommend missing business & technical capabilities (gap analysis)
description: From the intake inputs (business problem, desired outcome, known requirements — see ADP-zg3.2), the Requirements Intake screen should recommend the business capabilities and technical capabilities needed to solve the problem that are MISSING from the org's registries. Grounded gap analysis: compare the needed capabilities implied by the inputs against existing records — business capabilities (src/adp/business, business_capabilities) and technical capabilities (src/adp/application, technical_capabilities table; web/src/application/TechCapTree.tsx) — and surface the gaps (needed-but-absent) on the intake screen (web/src/intake/IntakePage.tsx). Should reuse the registry-grounding approach from ADP-SPEC-007 (see src/adp/recommendation/reuse.py) so recommendations cite existing capabilities and flag gaps rather than hallucinate. OPEN QUESTIONS: (a) LLM-assisted gap inference vs. deterministic matching; (b) do recommended-missing capabilities become draft records the architect can accept into the registry, or advisory-only; (c) how gaps are presented (list per business/technical, with rationale).
design: Likely a new analysis step that takes the intake inputs + queries the business/technical capability registries, then returns two lists: needed-and-present (reuse) and needed-but-missing (gap). Present on the intake screen alongside proposals. Consider letting the architect promote a recommended-missing capability into the registry (create business_capability / technical_capability) with provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Given intake inputs, the screen shows recommended business capabilities and technical capabilities, clearly marking which already exist (cited from the registry) and which are missing/gaps; missing ones are actionable or clearly advisory; covered by tests.
notes:
CAPABILITY ATTRIBUTE INVENTORY (captured 2026-07-16; updated with maturity + strategic relevance) — the two capability entities are ASYMMETRIC, so gap analysis must handle them separately:

BUSINESS capability (business_capabilities, SPEC-033/035): id, name(≤255,required), description(text,nullable), level(1|2|3 = HIERARCHY depth), parent_id(null@L1, required@L2/L3), position(int ordering), domain_id/domain_name(SPEC-035; null when unassigned or level>1), created_at, updated_at. App→biz-cap links carry fit_score(1-5). NEW attributes being added: maturity_level(1-5, business only) via ADP-4ga; strategic_relevance(1-3 Strategic/Core/Supporting) via ADP-33v.

TECHNICAL capability (technical_capabilities, SPEC-036): id, name(≤255,required), description(text,nullable), level(1|2|3 hierarchy, CHECK), parent_id(self-FK, ON DELETE RESTRICT), created_at. App→tech-cap links carry usage_type. NO position, NO domain, NO updated_at, NO maturity. NEW: strategic_relevance(1-3) via ADP-33v (applies to BOTH entities).

THREE numeric axes to keep straight: level (1-3 hierarchy), strategic_relevance (1-3 Strategic/Core/Supporting), maturity_level (1-5, business only). Distinct names + label maps required — see ADP-33v and ADP-4ga.

Implications for this gap-analysis bead: (1) searchable text for both = name + description only (already indexed by ADP-b6o); no aliases/synonyms/tags to match on. (2) Business caps carry the richest context (domain, maturity, strategic_relevance); technical caps carry strategic_relevance too. Gap analysis can exploit these — e.g. flag a needed capability that EXISTS but is low-maturity or classified Strategic-but-weak as a gap-of-strength/priority, not just presence/absence. (3) Do NOT confuse technical_capabilities (taxonomy) with element_technology_tags (SPEC-029, per-design element metadata: technology/vendor/platform/version/owner_team/free_tags) — different concept.
close_reason: Capability gap analysis shipped: GET /api/v1/designs/{id}/capability-gaps compares confirmed requirements against business/technical capability registries via deterministic keyword-overlap matching (reusing adp.recommendation.reuse), split into present (cited) vs missing (advisory gap). Web CapabilityGapPanel on the intake sidebar. PR opened.

title: Evaluate Pydantic AI as preferred framework for agentic components
description:
Why: ADP's agentic/LLM components have grown organically across four
features with three different approaches, all hand-rolled to varying
degrees, despite Pydantic v2 already being a core dependency everywhere in
the codebase:
  - adp.recommendation (007) + adp.judge (008): use langgraph>=0.2 +
    langchain-core>=0.2 (only src/adp/recommendation/orchestrator.py
    actually imports langgraph -- confirmed by grep, judge doesn't use it
    despite the dependency being installed).
  - adp.agents (039, Agent Review toolkit): deliberately built WITHOUT
    langgraph ("single-prompt reviewer, not a multi-node graph" --
    CLAUDE.md) -- a custom toolkit with its own grounding/provenance/
    citation-verification helpers.
  - adp.chat (041, AAI Chat Assistant): also deliberately custom --
    adp.llm.client.LLMClient hand-implements SSE parsing for BOTH Anthropic
    and OpenAI-compatible providers, hand-rolls the tool-use round-trip
    loop (orchestrator.py's _MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS loop), and hand-rolls
    structured-output validation via Pydantic models applied after the
    fact rather than at the framework level.

Pydantic AI (github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) is the Pydantic team's own
agent framework: type-safe tool calling, structured output validation
built on Pydantic v2 models directly (not bolted on after), streaming,
multi-provider support (Anthropic/OpenAI/others) without hand-rolling
provider-specific SSE parsing, and dependency-injection for
request-scoped context (sessions, auth) that maps naturally onto this
codebase's existing session-passing patterns (biz_session/app_session/
kb_session in adp.chat.orchestrator, for example).

What: research task, not an implementation commitment yet.
  1. Evaluate whether Pydantic AI would reduce/replace the hand-rolled
     parts of adp.llm.client (multi-provider SSE parsing) and
     adp.chat.orchestrator (tool-use loop) with less custom code to
     maintain, without losing anything the current design deliberately
     chose (e.g. adp.chat's per-question sensitive-data permission
     gating inside tool handlers, ADP-SPEC-041 research D5 -- confirm
     Pydantic AI's tool-calling model still allows enforcement INSIDE the
     tool function, not just at a framework layer).
  2. Evaluate it as a potential consolidation point across ALL FOUR
     existing approaches (langgraph-based recommendation/judge, and the
     two custom toolkits) rather than a fifth parallel pattern -- or
     conclude the existing split is intentional/fine and scope Pydantic AI
     to new work only.
  3. Check licensing, maturity/stability (versioning; this framework is
     younger than langgraph/langchain), and whether it changes the
     dual-provider (Anthropic + OpenAI-compatible) support story
     research D1 in specs/041-ai-chat-assistant/research.md chose raw
     httpx specifically to preserve.
  4. If promising, produce a small proof-of-concept against ONE existing
     component (adp.chat is the newest/smallest surface) before proposing
     a broader migration -- do not rewrite working, tested code on the
     strength of a framework evaluation alone.

Not yet spec'd via /speckit-specify -- this is a framework/architecture
research task, tracked here rather than as an ADP-SPEC-NNN feature.

Once the workflow file was live, its own push-triggered run (it matches its

principal, found and fixed by actually running it rather than assuming the
scopes I granted during setup were sufficient:

     logs, listBuildSourceUploadUrl, etc.) plus registries/read, nothing
     broader. Granted it scoped to the ACR resource, then REMOVED the now-
     redundant separate Reader grant (Tasks Contributor already includes
     registries/read) to keep RBAC minimal -- not left as overlap debt.
  3. Third run: SUCCEEDED end to end. Verified for real, not just "run
     passed": (a) the workflow's own /health smoke-test step logged
     "Healthy" after 2 cold-start retries (matches the already-known
     scale-to-zero behavior); (b) independently confirmed via
     'az containerapp show' that the live adp-api image tag
     (f0e1ee1aee46ac66ef31748c9af3432a449fe016) is the EXACT commit SHA of
     the triggering push, proving it deployed the real new image, not a
     stale one; (c) independently curled
     https://adp-api.lemondesert-3676f0a4.eastus2.azurecontainerapps.io/health
     myself from outside GitHub Actions -> 200 {"status":"healthy"}.

Final RBAC on the OIDC service principal (adp-github-actions-deploy):
AcrPush + Container Registry Tasks Contributor scoped to the ACR only,
Container Apps Contributor scoped to adp-rg only. No access to Postgres,
Key Vault, or networking. All three grants were arrived at by actually
running the pipeline and fixing what broke, not guessed upfront.
close_reason: CI/CD workflow verified working end-to-end via 3 real runs: found and fixed two genuine RBAC gaps (ACR control-plane read, ACR Tasks upload permission) beyond what was initially granted, then confirmed the deployed image tag matches the triggering commit and /health returns 200 independently.

title: SSO (Keycloak) unusable from Windows browser in WSL dev; keycloak-js double-init
description:
Running the app with auth enabled (ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=true / VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=true) shows a blank screen when opened from the Windows browser at localhost:5173. Diagnosed 2026-07-13 via headless Chromium: the SPA correctly redirects to the Keycloak login page, so the app is fine — the failure is the auth leg. Two problems:

1. NETWORK: Keycloak listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 (WSL loopback only), while Vite (*:5173) and the API (0.0.0.0:8001) are on all interfaces. keycloak-js redirects the Windows browser to http://127.0.0.1:8080/... which Windows cannot reach (loopback-bound, not forwarded) -> blank. Vite/API work from Windows because they bind all interfaces.

2. CODE: keycloak-js throws 'A Keycloak instance can only be initialized once' because React 18 StrictMode double-invokes the init effect in AuthProvider.tsx (initKeycloak called twice on the same instance). Console error; can blank the post-login return leg.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE: local dev runs no-auth via root .env (ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=false) and web/.env.local (VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false). App renders fully as the dev enterprise-architect.
design: Fix (1): bind Keycloak to 0.0.0.0:8080 for WSL dev (host-level Keycloak start config) so WSL2 localhost forwarding exposes it to Windows; verify http://127.0.0.1:8080 loads from the Windows browser. Fix (2): guard initKeycloak against double-init in web/src/auth/keycloak.ts or AuthProvider.tsx (module-level 'initialized' flag / promise memo, or keycloak.didInitialize check) so StrictMode's double effect is idempotent. Verify end-to-end: with both fixes + valid ADPRealm creds, login succeeds from Windows and the app renders.
acceptance_criteria: With auth enabled, opening localhost:5173 from Windows redirects to Keycloak, login succeeds, and the app renders (no blank screen, no 'initialized once' console error). No-auth workaround can then be removed (restore ADP_AUTH_ENABLED=true, delete web/.env.local).
